summary: Keep legacy dependency-wait tickets visible in read projections

delivery.outcome: Continue existing PLF-21260: keep the observed legacy waiting_dependency records PLF-21505/21507 visible in canonical read and SQLite projections as open tickets with execution.state waiting_dependency and preserved dependency edges. Version the disposable read projection so a previously current index is rebuilt for the repaired parser even when canonical files are unchanged.
nonGoals: Do not expand the canonical TicketStatus command enum, grant execution authority, clear dependencies or reactivate contradictory terminal execution states.
No canonical YAML/evidence rewrite during reads, data migration or unqualified Native activation.

architecture.decision: Normalize the narrowly observed legacy queue status only at Store read ingestion: preserve the wait in execution metadata, preserve existing executor/queue/blocked_by fields, and reject conflicting or malformed execution records through existing validation. Keep the write model strict. Include a private read-projection revision in the existing source signature; the maintenance guard rejects an old-generation index without modifying canonical sources.

dataChanges.description: The existing disposable SQLite projection gains the legacy records; canonical source bytes remain unchanged during reads.

architecture.rollback: Revert source; retain every canonical source record and history journal.

validation.evidence: Point/list/API/index read visibility, dependency/queue preservation, no source rewrites or invented executor; contradictory terminal records remain fail-closed and command enum stays strict. A preexisting4-part source signature is stale under the new read generation and one automatic repair restores omitted IDs.

commands: protected OneDev exact-head/current-base verification and independent Validator publication
validation.evidence: Independent source merge plus a separately qualified installed candidate restores full copied-source ID coverage before one Native rollout.
